$comment: Status per area: ported | partial | planned | wont-port | unknown. Notes and evidence are optional; evidence is a URL. Assessed against the repository, not docs claims: authored test suites, goldens captured from Pi 1.1.0, compatibility/*.v1.1.0 inventories and overlays, and compatibility/sync-1.1.0-applicability.json. deviations lists the differences that remain, intentional ones first.

promises.label: Behavioral parity
promises.blurb: Does PiSharp do what Pi does? Same prompts, tools, ordering and results for the same inputs.

rows.notes: Steering and follow-up queues with both drain modes, parallel tool batches, abort and automatic retry. turn_end drafts and message_end replacements apply inside the running loop, as in Pi.

rows.area: Built-in tools: read, write, edit, bash, grep, find, ls
rows.notes: Pi's declarations, arguments and errors. read returns images, decoded and resized with SkiaSharp. bash finds its shell as Pi does, with shellCommandPrefix and user_bash interception. grep and find use rg and fd, downloaded on first use. Difference: when your own !command shell can't start, the error text differs from Node's spawn error.

All 10 of Pi's chat APIs, including Bedrock, Codex and Copilot, and all 42 provider catalogs, each with a live route and /login. --model patterns, --models, --list-models, models.json and the startup catalog refresh work. Gaps: no llama.cpp router discovery and no /llama. Intentional: no Codex WebSocket, no zstd.

OpenAI decisions (with image input), TypeSafe and Cloudflare system-one, llama.cpp log-probability classification and OpenRouter images. Reachable from codemode, native extensions and TypeScript extensions, which can also register their own classifier and image providers.

Plain pisharp takes every flag in Pi's args.ts, with -p, --mode json|rpc, @file arguments and the install, remove, update, list, config, auth and mcp commands. Gaps: packages loaded with -e add their extensions but not their skills, prompts or themes; pisharp mcp ignores --offline and httpProxy. pisharp update can't update PiSharp itself.

Sessions in ~/.pi/agent/sessions, --continue, --resume, --session, --session-id, --fork, --session-dir and --no-session, /name, /session, /fork, /clone, /tree, /resume, HTML export and /share. Session files are compared with files Pi 1.1.0 wrote for the same scripts.
Manual and automatic compaction and branch summaries, with Pi's summary retries and their events.

All 24 of Pi's built-in commands, with the same names, descriptions and arguments, plus /mcp. /bug builds Pi's local report and opens a prefilled PiSharp GitHub issue instead of uploading to Pi's developers.

rows.area: Skills, prompt templates and context files
rows.notes: AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md from the agent folder and every parent folder, SYSTEM.md and APPEND_SYSTEM.md, and skills, prompts and themes discovered from Pi's folders and settings, behind project trust.

Pi's interactive mode on Windows, Linux and macOS: fullscreen and regular modes, every /settings item, the system, dark and light themes and custom theme files, keybindings.json, inline images, Mermaid and highlight.js highlighting. Gap: on Linux X11 the clipboard needs xclip or xsel; Pi also has a built-in helper.

Stdio and HTTP servers, ~/.pi/agent/mcp.json and the trusted project .pi/mcp.json, OAuth with refresh locks, all exposure modes, resource tools, the 10-second wait for direct servers, the mcp_servers prompt section, /mcp and pisharp mcp.
Pi's BM25 search, always registered and switched off as in Pi. It waits for background servers, and its prompt snippet is rendered.

Pi's prelude, script API, store, models bridge and limits, on the Jint engine. Codemode MCP servers connect. Intentional: each script runs in its own worker process (about 100 to 300 ms to start), its deadline starts when the script starts, and memory and recursion overruns end the script instead of throwing.

promises.label: Session & RPC compatibility
promises.blurb: Can PiSharp read and write the same files and speak the same protocol, so tools built for Pi keep working?

rows.notes: Reads JSONL v3 session trees and keeps unknown entries and fields. Difference: a line with an escaped lone surrogate, or nested deeper than 64 levels, stops the file from opening.
Every line is the bytes JSON.stringify writes, in Pi's key order. Compared entry by entry with session files captured from Pi 1.1.0.
Pi's own v1 and v2 migration on open, and session copy and session migrate, which leave the original file unchanged.
Every event Pi sends, including entry_appended, thinking_level_changed, extension_error, auto_retry_* and summarization_retry_*. agent_end carries willRetry.
All 33 Pi v1.1.0 RPC commands. Under pisharp --mode rpc, bash runs in your shell with no extra options.
select, confirm, input, editor, notify, setStatus, setWidget, setTitle and set_editor_text requests, and their responses.

Each line is read and written as rpc-mode.ts does. SIGTERM and SIGHUP shut down as in Pi. Differences: input nested deeper than 64 levels ends the stream, and escaped lone surrogates arrive as U+FFFD.
settings.json, auth.json, models.json, mcp.json, mcp-auth.json, keybindings.json and trust.json in ~/.pi/agent (or PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR), and the project .pi folder. !command values run, as in Pi.

promises.label: Extension compatibility
promises.blurb: Do Pi's TypeScript extensions and packages run unchanged? PiSharp runs them in Node with Pi's own npm packages, installed and verified on first use. Native C# extensions load from the same folders. The extension suite runs in the release pipeline with Node 22.

rows.notes: Discovered from ~/.pi/agent/extensions, .pi/extensions (after project trust), settings, packages and -e, as in Pi. Needs Node.js 22.13 or later; Pi asks for 22.19.

pi-coding-agent, pi-ai, pi-tui and pi-agent-core 1.1.0 are installed with your npm, checked against the registry's integrity, and loaded through Pi's jiti. Offline, or without npm, extensions fall back to built-in copies with a warning.
Every member: tools, commands, shortcuts, flags, providers (chat, classifier and image), virtual models, MCP servers and the event bus. Difference: ctx.ui.setTheme returns an error.

Every v1.1.0 extension event reaches TypeScript handlers. Difference: sendMessage with triggerTurn from inside a command starts its turn after the handler returns, and is dropped if the handler runs longer than about 30 seconds.
ctx.ui dialogs, widgets and custom components, registerMessageRenderer and registerToolRenderer, in the terminal UI and over RPC.
pisharp install, remove, update, list and config for npm, git and local sources, global or project (-l), with Pi's trust rules.

A folder with a pisharp-extension.json loads from the same places as Pi extensions, without Node, and shares the session and command list with TypeScript extensions. 39 of the 41 v1.1.0 events reach native handlers; project_trust and resources_discover reach only TypeScript extensions.

items.title: No telemetry
items.notes: PiSharp doesn't report installs to Pi's servers. PI_TELEMETRY and enableInstallTelemetry are accepted and ignored.

items.title: User agents
items.notes: Requests to Anthropic, Azure, Bedrock, Mistral, OpenAI-compatible endpoints and OpenRouter images send a PiSharp user agent where Pi's SDKs send their own.

items.title: Codemode worker
items.notes: Each script runs in its own worker process, so one script can't take PiSharp down. That costs about 100 to 300 ms per script. The deadline starts when the script starts running, not when the worker launches.

items.title: Jint limits
items.notes: Codemode runs on Jint, not QuickJS. Memory and recursion overruns end the script instead of throwing a catchable error, and the engine's own error messages differ.

items.title: No zstd
items.notes: .NET has no zstd encoder, so Codex requests are sent uncompressed.

items.title: No Codex WebSocket
items.notes: OpenAI Codex uses server-sent events only.

items.title: No self-update
items.notes: pisharp update updates packages and catalogs. Update PiSharp itself with dotnet tool update -g PiSharp.Cli.

deviations.title: Still open
deviations.blurb: Differences that remain to be fixed or decided.

items.title: Lone surrogates
items.notes: Output escapes them as JSON.stringify does. On input, RPC and tool-call arguments turn them into U+FFFD, and a session line that contains one is refused.

items.title: JSON depth 64
items.notes: Session records, RPC input and streamed tool-call arguments nested deeper than 64 levels are refused. JSON.parse has no such limit.

items.title: Fractional token counts
items.notes: Usage counts must be whole numbers. A provider that reports a fraction fails the response, and Bedrock reads it as 0.

items.title: Memory bounds
items.notes: PiSharp keeps byte bounds Pi doesn't have: 64 MiB per session line and session file, 16 MiB per streamed event and 64 MiB per response, 8 MiB per tool result, 32 MiB per RPC record.

items.title: triggerTurn during a command
items.notes: An extension's sendMessage with triggerTurn from inside a command runs after the command returns, not while it runs.

items.title: User bash start failures
items.notes: When your !command shell can't start, Windows shows "RPC command failed." and Linux and macOS report the shell's own error with exit code 127, where Pi shows Node's spawn error.

items.title: Linux X11 clipboard
items.notes: Pi has a built-in X11 clipboard helper. PiSharp needs xclip or xsel.

phases.title: Freeze the compatibility target
phases.notes: Pinned to Pi v1.1.0, with the command, RPC and event inventories refreshed. Release profiles (P1-04) are still open.

phases.title: Provider layer
phases.notes: All 10 of Pi's chat APIs and 42 provider catalogs, logins, classifiers and images.

phases.title: Agent loop and tools
phases.notes: Loop, all built-in tools with images, codemode and tool_search.

phases.title: Sessions
phases.notes: Pi's session folder and format, byte for byte, with branching, compaction, export and sharing.

phases.title: Headless RPC, then terminal UI
phases.notes: Pi's command line, print, JSON and RPC modes, and the interactive UI with every slash command.

phases.title: Native extension SDK
phases.notes: C# extensions load from Pi's extension folders. 39 of 41 events reach native handlers.

phases.title: Optional Node bridge
phases.notes: Runs any Pi extension and package on Pi's own npm packages.

phases.title: Hardening and packaging
phases.notes: The release pipeline runs 17 offline suites on Linux, including the extension suite with Node. Platform and security qualification are open.

phases.notes: tool_search shipped in 1.1.0.1. Everything else on this page ships in 1.1.0.2, in preparation.
